endorsements.title: CHAI AI governance frameworks (playbooks)
endorsements.quote: Where vendor training materials are available, evaluate them against these criteria and supplement where needed.

commentary.bottom_line: No study supplied for this map tests whether assessing vendor AI training and building internal capacity to fill gaps improves user preparedness or patient outcomes, and no study documents the hazard itself. The recommendation rests on a single framework endorsement from the CHAI governance playbooks.

perspectives.view: The evidence base contains zero studies that test the practice and zero studies that document the hazard. Under GRADE conventions, certainty cannot be rated above no direct evidence. The single support is a framework statement, which reflects expert judgment rather than measured effect.

The CHAI playbooks list this as a must, directing systems to evaluate vendor training materials against stated criteria and supplement them where needed. This is voluntary framework guidance. No supplied source ties it to an FDA, ONC, or state statutory requirement.

commentary.research_gap: Studies are needed that compare vendor-only training with vendor training plus locally developed material, measuring user competence, error rates, workflow fit, override behavior, and staff time. Separate work could establish how often vendor training is insufficient for local use, since no supplied study documents that hazard.
commentary.underserved_note: No study tested the practice, so no evidence covers Medicaid, safety-net, limited English proficiency, or low-literacy populations. Health systems serving these groups have no data on whether vendor training addresses their local workflows, interpreter use, or patient communication needs, and they may need to judge adequacy without outside benchmarks.
